objective: Review the scoped execution boundary for turning reviewed Verilator-process-to-launcher bridge fixture metadata into a wrapper-mediated Verilator-facing process plus structured launcher start, and decide whether a future run gate may attempt that path without treating this review as execution, compare, timing, broad native option support, arbitrary filelist support, automatic GPU allocation, runtime/ABI change, raw-state equality, direct Verilator sidecar execution, or production throughput evidence.

review_decision.reason: The definition is narrow enough for a first Verilator-facing process bridge run attempt because it starts from reviewed bridge fixture metadata, requires the expanded native option spelling, preserves explicit sidecar context and reviewed source/template authority, ties the bridge to exact process-to-launcher CLI metadata, and only permits the existing structured run_hybrid_template.py argv for pulp_ita_mha 64x1.
review_decision.weakest_point: This is still review-only. It does not start a Verilator-facing process, start the launcher, execute sidecar stages, record native-path compare, or measure timing. The strongest remaining risk is that a future run could merely prove parser acceptance plus an existing launcher run unless it records observable evidence that the wrapper-mediated Verilator-facing bridge path reached the launcher start in order.
accepted_because: the source definition is explicitly definition-only
the eligible input is limited to reviewed Verilator-process-to-launcher bridge fixture metadata
the future run must accept the expanded native option spelling before launcher start
the bridge metadata must be validated against reviewed process-to-launcher CLI metadata
explicit sidecar context source authority is required and unreviewed sidecar context refs must be rejected
the launcher argv is structured and exactly names python3, src/tools/run_hybrid_template.py, config/slice_launch_templates/pulp_ita_mha.json, --shape, and 64x1
success requires observable wrapper-mediated bridge evidence before launcher start
coverage_output_equivalence remains the only future correctness policy and raw full-state equality remains out of scope
generated reports and artifacts remain noncanonical evidence
